# External Comparative Evaluation — Recruitment Message

**Status: NOT SENT.** This is a template with placeholders. No reviewer has been recruited;
do not claim any are. Do not send until Walter approves the recipient list and the exact text.

## Purpose

Recruit 5–10 experienced product people to evaluate **blinded outputs** of a product-decision
skill pack, honestly and without obligation to share or star. The deliverable is feedback,
not endorsement.

## Selection criteria (build the list from these; do not invent names)

- Experienced PM or product leader (5+ years or Director/VP/Principal/founder-equivalent).
- Publicly interested in AI-assisted product work (they have written/talked/built in the area).
- Known to give critical feedback, not just promote.
- Varied seniority and product model (B2B / consumer / marketplace / developer tool / AI
  product / founder).
- No conflict of interest that would require them to endorse anything.

## List-building spec

- 15–20 candidates from the selection criteria above.
- Each entry: name/handle, role, why they fit the criteria, their public AI-PM interest
  (a link or reference), and their contact method.
- Verify the source of every name before any contact. No fabricated names.

## Outreach template (personalize per recipient; placeholders in [brackets])

Subject: Blinded PM-decision eval — 3 outputs, ~40 min, no strings

Hi [Name],

I maintain an open-source skill pack that gives AI agents an evidence-based product-decision
method (framing, discovery synthesis, experiment design, GO/NO-GO). I've seen you write about
[their specific AI-PM interest], so I'd like your critical eye — not your endorsement.

I'm running a blinded evaluation: for a set of realistic PM situations, I generate four
outputs from four different methods and ask reviewers to score them on decision usefulness,
evidence handling, confidence, ceremony, and actionability. Reviewers do not know which
method made which output.

The ask, if you have ~40 minutes:
- Evaluate three blinded examples (or more if you're willing).
- Report failures honestly — I explicitly want the outputs that are bad.
- No obligation to share, star, or promote anything.

You can read the rubric and form first:
[link to skills/evals/external/reviewer-rubric.md] and [reviewer-form.md]
[link to the scenarios directory]

Results will be published honestly, favorable or not. Want in?

Thanks,
[Your name]

## Response templates (after someone replies)

### Genuine question

> Good question. [answer, e.g. about how scenarios were written / what the four methods are /
> how blinding works]. Here's the relevant doc: [link]. Happy to clarify anything else.

### Skeptical criticism

> That's a fair criticism. [If it's about method: acknowledge, and note what the study can
> and cannot show at this sample size. If it's a specific output failure: record it as an
> open finding and thank them.] I'm publishing results honestly, so this is exactly the kind
> of feedback the study needs.

### Installation problem

> Thanks for telling me — installation failures are the highest-value feedback I get. Can you
> share [the command you ran / the error you saw / your agent and version]? I'll reproduce
> and fix it, and add it to the installation matrix.

### Competing resource recommendation

> Thanks — I'll look at [the resource]. If it does this better with less friction, that's
> exactly the kind of signal the evaluation is for, and I'd rather know than not.
